newsitem.title: UK: Austria bond seen around 3.0-5.0 bln French francs.
newsitem.headline: Austria bond seen around 3.0-5.0 bln French francs.

text.p: Austria's planned structured French franc Eurobond will likely be for 3.0-5.0 billion French francs, dealers close to the issue said.
They said pre-marketing had begun overnight, and the issue was being extremely well received.
The deal will be formally launched early next week, possibly Monday "if today's U.S. jobs data doesn't make the bond market lose a wheel," said one senior banker at a U.S. firm.
The Austrian bond will carry a 5.50 percent coupon and have a January 18, 2004, maturity, exactly matching the details on an existing Austrian government schilling bond.
Holders of the franc bond will have an option to exchange their bonds for the Austrian bund.

Austria will have an option to redenominate the franc bond in euros after France joins the single European currency. Austria may issue further bonds with a 5.50 percent coupon and January 2004 maturity in other core EMU currencies which it may also redenominate into euros.
These further core EMU currency Austrian bonds may also be exchanged for the Austrian bund by investors.
Austria will have an option to consolidate bonds from these issues which are not exchanged into one jumbo euro Eurobond.
The ultimate aim is to have either a "super liquid Austrian euro Bund or a super liquid euro Eurobond," one banker said.
